style: who is speaking to whom, and what has just happened

candidates.angle: anasyuh, without fault-finding, reveals the listener's inner state
shrunuyat, may listen, opens the door to liberation for anyone
api yo narah, even a person who, shows that listening alone is enough
candidates.evidence: अपि यो नरः (even a person who)

en.intro: Krishna finishes his teaching and opens the door to liberation beyond Arjuna. Listen to who else can enter.
en.notice: Listen to the word anasyuh, without fault-finding. The teaching does not demand a scholar, only a listener who comes without mockery to hear what is said.
en.next: Krishna asks Arjuna directly if his confusion is gone, closing the conversation he began.
en.meaning: Even a person who listens to this with trust and without fault-finding becomes free and reaches the auspicious realms earned by noble action.

hi.intro: कृष्ण अपनी शिक्षा समाप्त करते हैं और अर्जुन के अलावा भी मुक्ति का मार्ग खोलते हैं। सुनिए, और कौन इसमें प्रवेश पा सकता है।
hi.meaning: श्रद्धावान् और दोषरहित जो मनुष्य इस गीताग्रन्थ को सुन भी लेगा, वह भी सम्पूर्ण पापों से मुक्त होकर पुण्यकारियों के शुभ लोकों को प्राप्त हो जाएगा।
hi.notice: एक शब्द फिर सुनिए, अनसूयः, यानी दोषरहित। यह शिक्षा किसी विद्वान की माँग नहीं करती, केवल एक ऐसे श्रोता की माँग करती है जो उपहास या दोष निकालने की भावना से मुक्त होकर सुने।
hi.next: कृष्ण अर्जुन से सीधे पूछते हैं कि क्या उनकी उलझन दूर हो गई है, और उस बातचीत को समाप्त करते हैं जो उन्होंने शुरू की थी।

issues: meaning_changed: "बिना उपहास सुने कि क्या कहा जा रहा है" (The word 'anasyuh' means without fault-finding or without scoffing at the teaching/teacher. The Hindi phrase incorrectly translates it as 'without hearing mockery' (बिना उपहास सुने), which alters the meaning to imply the listener is the target of mockery rather than being free from a fault-finding attitude themselves.)

wrong_fact: "Listen to the word anasyuh, without fault-finding" (The Hindi word for 'without fault-finding' in the source is अनसूयः (anasuyah). The script spells it as 'anasyuh' and presents it as a Hindi word to listen to, which is a factual error regarding the exact term used in the verse.)
